title: Onboard Orion Lite 6B v1.2: performance profiles, metadata, and changelog automation
author: Miguel Ortega
description: This PR onboards the Oron Lite 6B v1.2 model into the model registry with updated metadata, a set of validated performance profiles, and automation to generate changelog/release notes entries. Motivation: v1.2 includes improved tokenizers and a memory-efficient attention kernel that affects latency and memory footprint; we want the registry to expose accurate profiles and automated changelog entries so downstream serving and Dedicated deployments can select the correct kernel and scaling profiles. Changes include: 1) new metadata JSON for orion-lite-6b v1.2 (model size, tokenizer, supported precisions, recommended quantization configs), 2) perf profiles for CPU/GPU variants (p99 latency, throughput per-GPU, batch-sizing recommendations), 3) integration with changelog automation pipeline so releases add a human-readable entry and link to perf artifacts, 4) test harness updates for perf validations, and 5) docs and sample config for Dedicated routing. Checklist: - [x] add metadata file and bump registry index - [x] add perf-profile YAMLs (gpu32, gpuA100, cpu-8core) - [x] add changelog metadata so automation can emit release note - [x] add unit tests for metadata schema - [x] add perf smoke test to CI - [x] update quickstart example to reference v1.2 Known limitations: memory usage depends on attention kernel selection which is handled at runtime; perf numbers are measured on internal benchmark lab (linked below) and may vary across customer hardware. Related work: Linear ENG-1412, ENG-1498, and PERF-502. Links: benchmark lab run: https://internal.redwood/bench/orn-lite-6b/v1.2

merge_commit_message: Onboard orion-lite-6b v1.2: metadata, perf profiles, changelog automation
release_notes:
- Onboard orion-lite-6b v1.2: updated tokenizer and memory-efficient attention kernel.
- Added validated performance profiles for GPU (A100, GPU32) and CPU 8-core.
- Introduced changelog automation entry so model releases produce standardized release notes.
- Added recommended quantization presets (q4_0, q5_1) and quickstart example for Dedicated.
notes: Perf numbers were validated on internal benchmark lab (ENG-1412). Changelog automation hooks into tools/changelog-automation and will publish a release note in the next pipeline run. Customers using pinned model revisions are unaffected; runtime will still select kernel variants based on hardware.
risk_assessment: Low. Changes are additive: new metadata and profiles do not modify existing model entries. Automation adds new artifacts but is gated behind CI and requires an is_release flag to publish.
